chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Bakr ibn Salih al-Razi, on the authority of Abi Salt al-Harawi, who said: 'I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him)'
about faith, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Faith is a conviction in the heart, a verbal expression by the tongue, and an action by the limbs. Faith is not [complete] unless it is thus.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three essential components of faith according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the comprehensive nature of faith by integrating internal conviction, verbal declaration, and physical action, a definition that aligns with the Shia doctrine of 'faith with action' as opposed to mere intellectual assent. This tripartite structure underscores the inseparability of belief and practice, reflecting the broader Shia scholarly consensus that faith is not static but is manifested through the limbs. The emphasis on 'jawarih' (limbs/limbs of action) highlights the physical dimension of worship and deeds as essential indicators of true iman.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-3 Muhammad ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Waleed - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on theauthority of Bakr ibn Salih al-Razi, on the authority of Abi Salt al-Harawi, “I asked Al-Ridha (s) about faith.
He (s) said, ‘Faith is belief in the heart, expression by the tongue and enacting by the body parts. Anything else would not be faith.’”
